q1: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2: SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM ( SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID, VIEW_DATE FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) >1 ORDER BY ID ASC ) A
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEW_DATE, VIEWER_ID HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) > 1 ORDER BY ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT DISTINCT ID FROM ( SELECT DISTINCT VIEWER_ID AS ID, VIEW_DATE FROM VIEWS GROUP BY VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT ARTICLE_ID) >1 ORDER BY ID ASC ) A
counterexample: INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-01'); INSERT INTO VIEWS (ARTICLE_ID, AUTHOR_ID, VIEWER_ID, VIEW_DATE) VALUES (1, 101, 201, '2023-01-02');
explanation: Q1 groups by VIEW_DATE and VIEWER_ID, while Q2 groups by VIEWER_ID and VIEW_DATE. This difference in grouping affects the results when there are multiple view dates for the same viewer on the same article.
counterexample_dsp: The test data should have a viewer who views the same article on two different dates. Q1 will count this as a single view for the viewer, while Q2 will count it as two separate views.
